title: 荷兰东印度公司成立
titleEn: Founding of the Dutch East India Company
what: 世界上第一家公开发行股票、可自由转让股份的跨国股份公司成立。
whatEn: The first multinational joint-stock company to issue publicly tradable shares was founded.
why: 远洋贸易风险巨大、需要长期巨额资本，合伙制无法承担，于是出现了有限责任与股份转让机制。
whyEn: Long-distance trade was risky and capital-hungry beyond partnership capacity, so limited liability and share transfer emerged.
impact: 催生了阿姆斯特丹证券交易所与近代资本市场，也为公司治理、审计与信息披露制度埋下伏笔。
impactEn: It spawned the Amsterdam stock exchange and modern capital markets, planting the seeds of corporate governance, audit and disclosure.

sources.label: 荷兰东印度公司历史档案研究
sources.labelEn: Historical research on the Dutch East India Company

title: 工业革命
what: 以蒸汽机、纺织机械与铁冶为代表，生产从家庭作坊转向工厂，人均产出首次摆脱长期停滞。
whatEn: Steam engines, mechanized textiles and iron shifted production from workshops to factories, and output per person first escaped long-run stagnation.
why: 产权与专利保护、煤炭与资本可得、农业剩余释放劳动力、科学与工艺结合，使突破在英国率先发生。
whyEn: Property rights and patents, coal and capital, an agricultural surplus freeing labor, and the marriage of science and craft let the breakthrough start in Britain.
impact: 奠定现代增长与城市化，重塑全球力量格局；也带来圈地、童工与污染等社会代价，催生后续劳工与环境制度。
impactEn: It laid the base for modern growth and urbanization and reset global power, while enclosure, child labor and pollution spurred later labor and environmental institutions.

sources.label: 克拉夫特《工业革命》
sources.labelEn: Crafts, The Industrial Revolution

title: 《国富论》出版
titleEn: The Wealth of Nations Is Published
what: 亚当·斯密系统论述分工、市场机制与自由贸易，经济学第一次成为独立学科。
whatEn: Adam Smith set out division of labour, market mechanisms and free trade, founding economics as a discipline.
why: 工业革命前夕，重商主义管制盛行，需要一套解释财富来源的新框架。
whyEn: On the eve of industrialisation, mercantilist controls prevailed and a new framework for the sources of wealth was needed.
impact: 确立了「市场协调分散决策」的核心命题，直接影响此后两百多年的经济政策与贸易秩序。
impactEn: Established the core proposition that markets coordinate dispersed decisions, shaping economic policy and trade for two centuries.

sources.label: 斯密《国富论》
sources.labelEn: Smith, The Wealth of Nations

title: 第一次现代经济危机
what: 投机性投资与信贷扩张后急剧收缩，多家银行倒闭，失业与破产同时上升。
whatEn: Speculative investment and credit expansion collapsed abruptly, banks failed and unemployment and bankruptcies rose together.
why: 新兴的银行体系与股票市场第一次把信贷、投资与情绪连成放大回路。
whyEn: For the first time the new banking system and stock market linked credit, investment and sentiment into an amplifying loop.
impact: 证明危机是工业化金融体系的常态特征，推动了公司法、银行监管与最后贷款人角色的讨论。
impactEn: Proved crises are a regular feature of industrial financial systems, prompting debate on company law, bank regulation and a lender of last resort.

sources.label: 英国 1825 年金融危机史料汇编
sources.labelEn: Compiled sources on the British crisis of 1825

title: 古典金本位形成
titleEn: The Classical Gold Standard Takes Shape
what: 主要经济体把本币与黄金固定挂钩，形成事实上的固定汇率体系。
whatEn: Major economies pegged their currencies to gold, creating a de facto fixed-rate system.
why: 贸易与投资扩张需要稳定的汇兑环境，而黄金被视为超越国家信用的锚。
whyEn: Expanding trade and investment needed exchange-rate stability, and gold was seen as an anchor beyond state credit.
impact: 促进了国际贸易与资本流动，但也限制了逆周期调控空间，最终在大萧条与战争冲击下瓦解。
impactEn: It boosted trade and capital flows while restricting countercyclical policy, and it fell apart under depression and war.

sources.label: 艾肯格林《金镣铐》
sources.labelEn: Eichengreen, Golden Fetters

title: 大萧条
what: 股市崩盘后信贷收缩、银行连锁倒闭，全球产出与物价深度下滑，失业率飙升。
whatEn: After the crash, credit contracted and banks failed in chains; global output and prices fell deeply and unemployment soared.
why: 货币紧缩、金本位约束、银行挤兑与贸易保护主义相互强化，政策失误放大了冲击。
whyEn: Monetary tightening, the gold standard, bank runs and protectionism reinforced each other, and policy errors amplified the shock.
impact: 催生了凯恩斯革命、存款保险、证券监管与布雷顿森林体系，重塑了此后八十年的宏观政策框架。
impactEn: It produced the Keynesian revolution, deposit insurance, securities regulation and Bretton Woods, reshaping macro policy for eighty years.

sources.label: 弗里德曼、施瓦茨《美国货币史》
sources.labelEn: Friedman & Schwartz, A Monetary History of the United States

title: 罗斯福新政
what: 大萧条下，联邦以公共工程、金融整顿、社保与监管扩张政府职能，试验需求管理的财政政策。
whatEn: Amid the Depression, the federal government expanded through public works, financial repair, social security and regulation, testing demand-management fiscal policy.
why: 市场自发调整失灵、失业与通缩深重，凯恩斯式以支出补需求的思路与政治压力共同推动干预。
whyEn: Self-correction failed amid mass unemployment and deflation; Keynesian spending-to-fill-demand ideas and political pressure drove intervention.
impact: 建立存款保险、证券监管与社保体系，塑造现代福利国家雏形；其对增速的实际拉动至今仍有争议。
impactEn: It built deposit insurance, securities regulation and social security—prototypes of the modern welfare state—though its real pull on growth remains debated.

sources.label: 班克罗夫特《大萧条与新政》
sources.labelEn: Bancroft, The Great Depression and the New Deal

title: 《就业、利息和货币通论》出版
what: 凯恩斯提出总需求不足会导致持续失业，宏观经济学由此诞生。
whatEn: Keynes argued insufficient aggregate demand causes persistent unemployment, and macroeconomics was born.
why: 古典理论无法解释大萧条后的长期高失业，需要一套以总量需求为核心的新框架。
whyEn: Classical theory could not explain persistent mass unemployment, so a framework centred on aggregate demand was needed.
impact: 战后三十年财政与货币政策成为调控常态，并演化为今天的新凯恩斯主义模型。
impactEn: For three decades fiscal and monetary policy became routine tools, evolving into today's New Keynesian models.

sources.label: 凯恩斯《就业、利息和货币通论》
sources.labelEn: Keynes, The General Theory

title: 布雷顿森林体系确立
titleEn: The Bretton Woods System Is Established
what: 美元与黄金挂钩、其他货币与美元挂钩的固定汇率体系建立，并成立 IMF 与世界银行。
whatEn: A fixed-rate system pegged the dollar to gold and other currencies to the dollar, with the IMF and World Bank created.
why: 战后重建需要稳定汇率与融资渠道，同时要避免重蹈 1930 年代竞争性贬值的覆辙。
whyEn: Reconstruction needed stable rates and financing while avoiding a repeat of 1930s competitive devaluation.
impact: 带来近三十年的贸易扩张与相对稳定，同时确立了以 IMF 为核心的国际货币协调机制。
impactEn: It delivered nearly three decades of trade expansion and relative stability and established IMF-centred monetary coordination.

sources.label: IMF 布雷顿森林体系历史档案
sources.labelEn: IMF historical archives on Bretton Woods

title: 尼克松冲击：美元与黄金脱钩
titleEn: The Nixon Shock: the Dollar Leaves Gold
what: 美国单方面停止美元兑换黄金，布雷顿森林体系固定汇率基础崩塌。
whatEn: The United States suspended dollar convertibility into gold, destroying the fixed-rate basis of Bretton Woods.
why: 长期财政赤字与海外美元债务使黄金储备不足以支撑承诺兑换。
whyEn: Persistent deficits and overseas dollar liabilities left gold reserves unable to honour convertibility.
impact: 世界进入信用货币与浮动汇率时代，货币政策获得更大空间，也带来更高的通胀风险。
impactEn: The world entered the fiat-money and floating-rate era: more monetary room and higher inflation risk.

sources.label: 美联储历史档案 1971 年公告
sources.labelEn: Federal Reserve historical records, 1971 announcement

title: 第一次石油危机
what: 石油禁运与价格暴涨数倍，工业国同时出现高通胀与经济停滞。
whatEn: An oil embargo and a multi-fold price rise hit industrial economies with inflation and stagnation at once.
why: 地缘冲突触发供给中断，而需求短期缺乏弹性，涨价压力迅速传导到全产业链。
whyEn: Geopolitical conflict cut supply while demand was inelastic in the short run, transmitting price pressure across supply chains.
impact: 「滞胀」成为现实，凯恩斯式需求管理失效，理论与政策转向货币主义与供给侧。
impactEn: 'Stagflation' became real, Keynesian demand management failed and thinking turned to monetarism and supply-side policy.

sources.label: IEA 石油危机回顾报告
sources.labelEn: IEA retrospective on the oil crises

title: 中国改革开放启动
titleEn: China Launches Reform and Opening Up
what: 以家庭联产承包、设立经济特区与逐步放开价格、外贸与外资管制为起点，中国从高度集中的计划经济体向市场化转型。
whatEn: Beginning with household responsibility, special economic zones and gradually relaxing controls on prices, trade and foreign investment, China shifted from a centrally planned economy toward the market.
why: 计划经济下的短缺与效率瓶颈难以为继，需要引入市场激励与对外开放来释放生产力。
whyEn: Shortages and inefficiency under planning became unsustainable, so market incentives and opening up were needed to unleash productivity.
impact: 此后四十余年实现了高速工业化与大规模减贫，同时也伴随收入与区域差距、环境与债务等难题，是从计划到市场的标志性转折。
impactEn: It delivered rapid industrialisation and mass poverty reduction over the next four decades, alongside challenges of inequality, the environment and debt — a landmark turn from plan to market.

sources.label: 世界银行 中国改革开放四十年回顾
sources.labelEn: World Bank, China 40 Years of Reform and Development

title: 沃尔克紧缩
what: 美联储把政策利率提高到 20% 上下的历史高位，以两年深度衰退换取通胀回落。
whatEn: The Federal Reserve raised policy rates towards 20%, accepting a deep two-year recession to break inflation.
why: 通胀预期已经根深蒂固，只有足够强烈的紧缩才能重建央行可信度。
whyEn: Inflation expectations had become entrenched, so only decisively severe tightening could rebuild credibility.
impact: 通胀预期被锚定，奠定了此后四十年央行独立性与通胀目标制的制度共识。
impactEn: Expectations were anchored, establishing a forty-year consensus on central bank independence and inflation targeting.

sources.label: 美联储联邦基金利率历史数据
sources.labelEn: Federal Reserve historical federal funds rate data

title: 新自由主义转向
what: 撒切尔与里根推行私有化、放松管制、削减税率与控通胀，国家退、市场进成为政策主旋律。
whatEn: Thatcher and Reagan pushed privatization, deregulation, tax cuts and inflation control; the state retreated as the market advanced.
why: 滞胀暴露凯恩斯共识乏力，货币主义与供给学派崛起，工会式微为改革提供政治窗口。
whyEn: Stagflation exposed the limits of the Keynesian consensus; monetarism and supply-side economics rose while union decline opened a political window.
impact: 提升效率与资本回报、压低通胀，但也加剧不平等与金融不稳定，影响延续至今的全球政策辩论。
impactEn: It lifted efficiency and returns and tamed inflation but deepened inequality and financial instability, still shaping global policy debate.

sources.label: 哈维《简短的新自由主义史》
sources.labelEn: Harvey, A Brief History of Neoliberalism

title: 广场协议
what: 五国联合干预外汇市场，推动美元对日元与马克大幅贬值。
whatEn: Five countries jointly intervened in currency markets, driving a sharp depreciation of the dollar against the yen and mark.
why: 美国贸易逆差与保护主义压力上升，希望通过汇率调整而非关税解决失衡。
whyEn: With a widening US trade deficit and rising protectionism, exchange-rate adjustment was preferred to tariffs.
impact: 日元快速升值长期影响日本产业与资产价格，成为讨论汇率协调与资产泡沫的经典案例。
impactEn: The yen's rapid appreciation shaped Japanese industry and asset prices, making it a classic case in exchange-rate coordination and bubbles.

sources.label: 广场协议联合声明全文
sources.labelEn: Plaza Accord joint statement

title: 黑色星期一
what: 1987 年 10 月 19 日，道琼斯工业指数单日下跌 22.6%，创下一战以来最大的单日百分比跌幅，全球股市同步崩落，香港股市为此休市一周。
whatEn: On 19 October 1987 the Dow Jones fell 22.6 percent in a single session, its largest one-day percentage drop since the First World War, as markets worldwide collapsed together and Hong Kong suspended trading for a week.
why: 「投资组合保险」等程序化策略在下跌时机械卖出，形成自我强化的正反馈；同期美国财政与贸易赤字高企、利率上行、美元贬值预期升温，广场协议后的政策共识出现动摇，估值与机制在同一时刻反向。
whyEn: Mechanical strategies such as portfolio insurance sold as prices fell, creating a self-reinforcing loop, while large US fiscal and trade deficits, rising rates, a weakening dollar and fraying consensus after the Plaza Accord turned valuation and mechanism against each other at the same moment.
impact: 事件直接催生个股与指数层面的熔断机制、清算与保证金改革，以及央行「随时提供流动性」的公开承诺（美联储次日即发声明）。此后每一次技术性下跌，政策反应模板都源自 1987 年。
impactEn: It produced circuit breakers at both stock and index level, clearing and margin reform, and the explicit promise of central-bank liquidity — the Federal Reserve issued a supportive statement the next day. Every subsequent technical selloff has been managed against the 1987 template.

sources.label: 布雷迪委员会《1987 年 10 月 19 日股市下跌》报告（1988）
sources.labelEn: Brady Commission, Report of the Presidential Task Force on the Market Break of 19 October 1987 (1988)

title: 日本泡沫破裂
what: 股市与地价在广场协议后巨幅膨胀，1989–1991 先后破裂，日本陷入长期低增长与通缩的「失去的十年」。
whatEn: Equities and land ballooned after the Plaza Accord, then burst in 1989–1991, plunging Japan into a 'lost decade' of low growth and deflation.
why: 宽松货币与信贷扩张推高资产，银行与企业过度负债、期限错配，破裂后资产负债表受损抑制支出。
whyEn: Easy money and credit inflated assets; over-leveraged firms and banks and maturity mismatch meant a balance-sheet slump suppressed spending after the crash.
impact: 成为资产负债表衰退与长期通缩的经典案例，警示资产泡沫与政策迟滞，深刻影响后来的危机应对。
impactEn: It became the textbook case of a balance-sheet recession and prolonged deflation, warning on bubbles and slow policy, shaping later crisis response.

sources.label: 辜朝明《资产负债表衰退》
sources.labelEn: Koo, The Holy Grail of Macroeconomics

title: 黑色星期三：索罗斯做空英镑
titleEn: Black Wednesday: Soros Breaks the Bank of England
what: 1992 年 9 月 16 日，英镑被迫退出欧洲汇率机制（ERM）并大幅贬值。英国央行在一天内两次加息、动用数百亿美元干预仍然失败，索罗斯的量子基金当日获利约 10 亿美元，被称为「击垮英格兰银行的人」。
whatEn: On 16 September 1992 sterling was forced out of the Exchange Rate Mechanism and devalued sharply. The Bank of England raised rates twice in one day and spent billions defending the parity and still lost, while Soros's Quantum Fund made roughly USD 1 billion and earned the label 'the man who broke the Bank of England'.
why: 两德统一后德国为抑制统一带来的通胀维持高利率，欧共体成员国为守住汇率平价被迫跟随，而英国正陷衰退、失业高企——「为外部平价牺牲国内利率」在政治上不可持续。固定平价与基本面冲突时，投机者找到了一个可验证的错误定价。
whyEn: After German reunification the Bundesbank kept rates high to contain inflation, and EC members had to follow to hold their parities, while Britain sat in recession with mass unemployment: surrendering domestic rates to an external peg was politically untenable. Where a fixed parity contradicts fundamentals, speculators find a verifiable mispricing.
impact: 英镑兑马克贬值约三成，英国反而在低利率与宽松货币中开启九十年代的增长；意大利里拉退出机制、法郎被迫调整，法国国内对「德国中心」的怀疑加深。事件留下两条长期结论：央行干预难以对抗基本面，以及单一货币若缺少财政与危机应对安排会极其脆弱——这直接塑造了后来欧元区的收敛标准与危机制度设计。
impactEn: Sterling fell about thirty percent against the mark, and Britain entered the 1990s expansion with lower rates and easier money; the lira left the mechanism and the franc was realigned, deepening French suspicion of a German-centred system. Two conclusions endured: intervention cannot beat fundamentals, and a single currency without fiscal and crisis-capacity design is fragile — lessons that shaped the euro area's convergence criteria and its later crisis architecture.

sources.label: 英国上议院财政委员会关于 ERM 退出事件的报告（1997）
sources.labelEn: House of Lords Economic Affairs Committee report on leaving the ERM (1997)

sources.label: 索罗斯《金融炼金术》
sources.labelEn: George Soros, The Alchemy of Finance

title: 亚洲金融危机
what: 货币与资产价格暴跌，短期外债无法续借，多国被迫求助国际救助并陷入深度衰退。
whatEn: Currencies and asset prices collapsed, short-term foreign debt could not be rolled over and countries sought international rescue.
why: 固定汇率、大量短期外币借款与本币资产之间的期限和货币错配，一旦资本外流便迅速崩溃。
whyEn: Pegged rates, large short-term foreign borrowing and local-currency assets created currency and maturity mismatch that unravelled on outflows.
impact: 亚洲多国转向浮动汇率与外汇储备积累，IMF 的救助条件也引发广泛争论与改革。
impactEn: Many Asian economies moved to floating rates and reserve accumulation, and IMF conditionality came under intense debate and reform.

sources.label: IMF 亚洲金融危机专题评估
sources.labelEn: IMF assessments of the Asian financial crisis

title: 俄罗斯债务违约与卢布危机
titleEn: The Russian Default and Ruble Crisis
what: 1998 年 8 月 17 日，俄罗斯宣布扩大卢布汇率波动区间、暂停部分本币国债（GKO）偿付并重组外债，事实上的违约引发全球避险：风险利差飙升，各国股市下挫，高杠杆对冲基金被击穿。
whatEn: On 17 August 1998 Russia widened the ruble's trading band, suspended payment on part of its domestic short-term government paper (GKO) and restructured external debt. The de facto default triggered a global flight to quality: risk premia blew out, equities fell worldwide and leveraged hedge funds were pierced.
why: 亚洲金融危机与油价下跌同时打击俄罗斯的出口与资本流入，1995-1997 年以超短期国债和三位数利率维系的滚动融资本就依赖信心；财政赤字与税收征管失效使展期在 1998 年夏天断裂。
whyEn: The Asian crisis and collapsing oil prices hit Russia's exports and inflows together, while the pyramid of ultra-short bills rolled at triple-digit rates after 1995 depended entirely on confidence; a fiscal deficit and failed tax administration broke the rollover in the summer of 1998.
impact: 俄罗斯银行体系与居民储蓄遭到重创，此后靠本币贬值与油价回升才恢复增长。对全球而言，它成为新兴市场主权风险、热钱外逃与「 correlated trade 拥挤」的经典教材，并直接促成对美国长期资本管理公司（LTCM）的救助式清算与关于杠杆、集中清算的监管讨论。
impactEn: Russia's banking system and household savings were devastated, and recovery came only through devaluation and rising oil. For the world it became the textbook case of sovereign risk, hot-money flight and crowded correlated trades, prompting the supervised wind-down of Long-Term Capital Management and the debate on leverage and central clearing.

sources.label: 国际货币基金组织《俄罗斯与 1998 年危机》评估材料
sources.labelEn: IMF assessment materials on Russia and the 1998 crisis

sources.label: 美国总统工作市场工作组《长期资本管理公司的教训》（1999）
sources.labelEn: President's Working Group on Financial Markets, Lessons of LTCM (1999)

title: 欧元启动
what: 多国以单一货币启动经济与货币联盟，汇率风险消失，但货币政策交由欧洲央行统一制定。
whatEn: Several states launched economic and monetary union on one currency, erasing exchange-rate risk but handing monetary policy to a single ECB.
why: 以共同货币深化一体化、降低交易成本并制衡美元，被视为政治与经济双重工程。
whyEn: A common currency was meant to deepen integration, cut transaction costs and offset the dollar—a project both political and economic.
impact: 贸易与金融融合加深，但财政不统一遇上非对称冲击埋下隐患，直接酿成后来的欧债危机。
impactEn: Trade and finance integrated more deeply, but unified money over divided treasuries and asymmetric shocks sowed the seeds of the euro-area crisis.

sources.label: 德格拉韦《镜中的欧洲》
sources.labelEn: De Grauwe, Economics of Monetary Union

title: 中国加入世界贸易组织
titleEn: China Joins the World Trade Organization
what: 中国结束十五年复关与入世谈判，正式成为 WTO 成员，承诺大幅降低关税并削减非关税壁垒。
whatEn: After fifteen years of negotiations, China acceded to the WTO, committing to steep tariff cuts and reduced non-tariff barriers.
why: 融入多边贸易体系被视为以外部规则倒逼国内改革、并换取稳定出口市场的途径。
whyEn: Joining the multilateral system was seen as using external rules to push domestic reform while securing stable export markets.
impact: 出口与制造业产能快速扩张，中国深度嵌入全球产业链；同时也带来了产业冲击、贸易摩擦与对外依赖的讨论。
impactEn: Exports and manufacturing capacity expanded rapidly and China became deeply embedded in global supply chains; it also sparked debate on industry shocks, trade friction and external dependence.

sources.label: WTO 中国加入议定书
sources.labelEn: WTO Protocol on the Accession of China

title: 全球金融危机
what: 次贷违约引发抵押证券暴跌，大型金融机构倒闭或被救助，全球信贷市场冻结。
whatEn: Subprime defaults crashed mortgage securities, major institutions failed or were rescued, and global credit markets froze.
why: 高杠杆、复杂证券化、期限错配与监管盲区叠加，把局部房贷风险放大为系统风险。
whyEn: High leverage, complex securitisation, maturity mismatch and regulatory blind spots amplified local mortgage risk into systemic risk.
impact: 催生宏观审慎监管、压力测试与《巴塞尔协议 III》，并开启长达十余年的低利率与量化宽松时代。
impactEn: It produced macroprudential regulation, stress testing and Basel III, and opened a decade-long era of low rates and quantitative easing.

sources.label: 美国金融危机调查委员会最终报告
sources.labelEn: US Financial Crisis Inquiry Commission final report

title: 欧元区主权债务危机
what: 2010 年起希腊、爱尔兰、葡萄牙相继要求外部救助，西班牙与意大利国债收益率被推至不可持续的水平；希腊经历三轮官方救助与 2012 年的债务重组，同年 7 月欧央行行长德拉吉以「在职责范围内不惜一切代价」的表态稳住市场预期。
whatEn: From 2010 Greece, Ireland and Portugal requested external bailouts while Spanish and Italian bond yields were pushed to unsustainable levels; Greece went through three official programmes and a 2012 debt restructuring, and in July 2012 ECB President Draghi steadied expectations with his pledge to do 'whatever it takes' within the mandate.
why: 货币联盟统一了利率却没有统一财政与银行监管：入盟后南欧国家融资成本骤降，积累大量公共与私人债务与外部失衡；全球金融危机把银行私人债务转成公共债务，而「成员国国债无法由本国央行印钞支持」的制度缺陷在恐慌中暴露。
whyEn: The currency union equalised interest rates without unifying fiscal policy or banking supervision: after entry, southern members enjoyed sharply lower funding costs and accumulated public and private debt and external imbalances; the global crisis converted private bank debt into public debt, and the design flaw — no lender of last resort for member-state sovereigns — was exposed under panic.
impact: 欧元区建立欧洲金融稳定机制与欧洲稳定机制（ESM）、推出直接交易（OMT）、并走向银行业单一监管与清算机制；南欧国家经历深度衰退、青年失业率长期高企，关于紧缩有效性与共同债务的争论延续至今。「不完整的货币联盟」成为此后所有欧元区改革的出发点。
impactEn: The euro area built the EFSF and then the ESM, announced Outright Monetary Transactions, and moved towards banking union with single supervision and resolution; southern economies suffered deep recessions and persistently high youth unemployment, and the argument over austerity and common debt continues. 'An incomplete monetary union' became the premise of every subsequent euro-area reform.

title: 闪电崩盘
what: 2010 年 5 月 6 日下午，美股在约 36 分钟内集体跳水，标普 500 成分股一度下跌近 9%，宝洁等蓝筹瞬间以接近 1 美元的价格成交，随后大部分反弹；事后认定由一笔大型算法卖单引发。
whatEn: On the afternoon of 6 May 2010 US equities plunged over roughly thirty-six minutes, the S&P 500 fell nearly nine percent at the trough, blue chips such as Procter & Gamble traded momentarily near one dollar, and most of the move then reversed; a single large algorithmic sell order was identified as the trigger.
why: 订单簿深度依赖高频交易商，而它们在波动陡增时按风控规则撤出，流动性瞬间蒸发；跨现货与期货的套利与止损联动把一次普通的宏观数据交易放大成全面踩踏。
whyEn: Order-book depth depended on high-frequency firms that withdrew under their own risk rules once volatility spiked, so liquidity evaporated in minutes; arbitrage and stop-loss linkages across cash and futures amplified an ordinary macro trade into a stampede.
impact: 美英监管随后推出涨跌停带（limit up-down）、更明确的市场层面熔断与错误交易撤销规则，把高频交易纳入登记与风控要求，并推动「统一代码」与交易前风险评估。此后 2015 年、2018 年、2024 年等多次瞬时波动，都以本案为参照。
impactEn: US and UK regulators introduced limit-up/limit-down bands, clearer market-wide circuit breakers and broken-trade rules, brought high-frequency trading under registration and risk requirements, and pushed for a consolidated tape. Every subsequent burst of intraday volatility — 2015, 2018, 2024 — has been assessed against this case.

title: 中国股市异常波动
what: 上证指数 2015 年 6 月 12 日冲上 5178 点后，三周内下跌约三成，出现多次「千股跌停」；监管清理场外配资触发集中平仓，随后下调印花税、暂缓新股发行并组织证券公司资金入市稳定市场。
whatEn: After the Shanghai Composite peaked at 5178 on 12 June 2015 it fell about thirty percent in three weeks, with repeated sessions in which a thousand stocks hit the down limit. The crackdown on off-exchange margin lending triggered forced liquidation; the state then cut stamp duty, paused new listings and mobilised broker funds to stabilise the market.
why: 这轮上涨主要由融资融券与结构化配资带来的杠杆资金和宽松流动性推动，而非盈利改善；当监管要求清理杠杆，平仓与下跌互为因果，涨跌停加 T+1 的机制在流动性枯竭时把个体风险变成集体踩踏。
whyEn: The rally was driven by leverage — exchange margin and structured off-exchange financing — plus loose liquidity rather than earnings. When regulators required the leverage to be unwound, forced selling and falling prices caused each other, and price limits with T+1 settlement turned individual risk into a collective stampede when liquidity dried up.
impact: 事件推动中国加强对场外配资与股指期货的监管，2016 年初试行熔断机制又在四日内紧急叫停，成为「以机制抑制波动」的失败样本；同时留下关于政府直接入市稳定市场的边界、道德风险与政策退出成本的长期争论。
impactEn: It tightened supervision of off-exchange leverage and index futures; a circuit-breaker scheme launched in early 2016 was suspended within days, becoming a case study in trying to legislate away volatility. It also left an enduring argument about the limits of direct state market support, moral hazard and the cost of policy exit.

title: 瑞士央行放弃欧元汇率下限
titleEn: The SNB Drops the Euro Floor
what: 2015 年 1 月 15 日，瑞士央行突然宣布取消自 2011 年 9 月起执行的瑞郎兑欧元 1.20 下限并把超额准备金利率降至 -0.75%，瑞郎盘中升值逾 20%，全球外汇市场与使用高杠杆的经纪客户出现巨额亏损。
whatEn: On 15 January 2015 the Swiss National Bank abruptly scrapped the EUR/CHF 1.20 floor it had defended since September 2011 and cut its excess-reserve rate to minus 0.75 percent. The franc surged more than twenty percent intraday, inflicting heavy losses on the global currency market and on leveraged retail clients.
why: 为对抗避险资金涌入造成的通缩压力，SNB 三年间以近乎无上限的规模买入欧元维持价格下限；随着欧央行量化宽松预期升温，维持下限所需的干预规模与央行资产负债表、政治承受力之间的矛盾已不可持续。
whyEn: To resist deflationary pressure from safe-haven inflows the SNB had bought euros on an almost unlimited scale for three years; as expectations of ECB quantitative easing built, the intervention required to hold the floor had become incompatible with the size of its balance sheet and with political tolerance.
impact: 事件成为「央行政策承诺随时可撤销」的教科书案例：多家做市商与零售经纪商因穿仓被客户索赔，止损单集中滑点引发集体诉讼与监管检讨，零售外汇杠杆随后普遍下调。它也提醒所有以固定汇率为锚的经济体：锚的可靠性取决于维持它的成本。
impactEn: It became the textbook case of a central-bank promise that can be withdrawn at any moment: market-makers and retail brokers faced client claims for negative balances, stop-loss slippage produced class actions and supervisory reviews, and retail forex leverage was cut across the industry. Its wider warning to any economy anchored to a fixed rate is that the anchor is only as credible as the cost of defending it.

title: 疫情冲击与空前宽松
titleEn: The Pandemic Shock and Unprecedented Easing
what: 供给与需求同时停摆，各国推出史无前例的财政转移与资产购买计划。
whatEn: Supply and demand halted together, and governments launched unprecedented fiscal transfers and asset purchases.
why: 封控直接切断供给，收入骤降又冲击需求，需要「直达居民」的财政手段以避免资产负债表崩塌。
whyEn: Lockdowns cut supply while income collapse hit demand, requiring direct-to-household fiscal support to prevent balance-sheet collapse.
impact: 避免了债务通缩式萧条，但也带来后续通胀压力、财政债务上升与央行资产负债表大幅扩张。
impactEn: It avoided a debt-deflationary slump but left higher inflation, larger public debt and greatly expanded central bank balance sheets.

sources.label: IMF 财政监测 2021 年疫情应对评估
sources.labelEn: IMF Fiscal Monitor, pandemic response assessment

title: 全球通胀与快速加息
titleEn: The Global Inflation Surge and Rapid Hiking
what: 多国通胀升至数十年高位，主要央行以历史级速度加息，资产估值与房地产明显承压。
whatEn: Inflation hit multi-decade highs in many countries and major central banks hiked at historic speed, pressuring valuations and housing.
why: 供给冲击、需求结构变化与劳动力紧张叠加，使通胀从局部品类扩散为核心通胀。
whyEn: Supply shocks, shifted demand composition and tight labour markets spread inflation from individual categories into core measures.
impact: 再度验证央行可信度与通胀预期管理的重要性，也让「滞胀风险」重新回到政策讨论中心。
impactEn: It re-confirmed the importance of credibility and expectation management and returned stagflation risk to policy debate.

sources.label: BIS 年度经济报告 通胀与加息章节
sources.labelEn: BIS Annual Economic Report, inflation and policy chapter

title: 英国「迷你预算」与国债风暴
what: 2022 年 9 月 23 日，英国政府公布未经预算责任办公室评估的大规模无资金支持的减税方案，长期国债收益率急升、英镑跌至历史低位；养老金负债驱动型投资（LDI）被迫抛售国债，英格兰银行宣布紧急购债，三日后主要措施被撤回，首相两个月后去职。
whatEn: On 23 September 2022 the government announced a large package of unfunded tax cuts that had not been assessed by the Office for Budget Responsibility. Long-dated gilt yields spiked, sterling hit a record low, pension schemes using liability-driven investing were forced to sell gilts, the Bank of England launched emergency purchases, the flagship measures were reversed within days, and the Prime Minister left office two months later.
why: 在通胀接近两位数、央行正在加息的时刻推出扩张性财政，市场同时重新定价英国的通胀路径、主权信用与央行独立性；而 LDI 结构以高杠杆持有长期国债对冲养老金负债，收益率上升触发保证金追缴，被迫卖出又推高收益率，形成金融稳定问题。
whyEn: Expansionary fiscal policy at a moment of near-double-digit inflation and rising rates made markets reprice the UK's inflation path, sovereign credibility and central-bank independence at once; meanwhile LDI structures held long gilts on leverage to hedge pension liabilities, so higher yields triggered margin calls, and the resulting forced selling pushed yields further — turning a fiscal decision into financial stability risk.
impact: 事件促使英国对养老金 LDI 建立登记、压力测试与流动性缓冲要求，厘清了央行在国债市场既是监管者又可能是「最后交易人」的角色边界；也让「财政可信度本身就是利率的一部分」成为各国政策讨论中的通用教训。
impactEn: It produced registration, stress testing and liquidity buffers for pension LDI, clarified the boundary of the central bank's role as occasional market maker of last resort in gilts, and established the general lesson that fiscal credibility is itself a component of the interest rate.

title: 硅谷银行倒闭
titleEn: The Collapse of Silicon Valley Bank
what: 2023 年 3 月 10 日，硅谷银行被加州监管机构接管，成为美国当时第二大的银行倒闭事件。此前 48 小时内储户提取约 420 亿美元，其持有的长久期国债与住房抵押贷款支持证券在加息中浮亏，且缺乏稳定核心存款与利率对冲。
whatEn: On 10 March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank was seized by California regulators, then the second-largest bank failure in US history. Depositors had withdrawn about USD 42 billion in forty-eight hours; the bank held long-duration Treasuries and mortgage-backed securities sitting on unrealised losses after rapid rate hikes, without a stable core deposit base or interest-rate hedges.
why: 2020-2021 年科创企业存款激增，资金被配置到期限更长、收益更低的「安全」资产；2022 年激进加息同时造成两件事——资产端浮亏扩大，负债端初创企业加速提款。久期错配在融资与信心同时收紧时暴露，而社交媒体把挤兑速度提高了几个数量级。
whyEn: Deposit inflows from tech firms in 2020-2021 were placed in longer-dated, lower-yielding 'safe' assets. Aggressive 2022 rate hikes did two things at once: unrealised losses grew on the asset side while startups drew down cash on the liability side. Duration mismatch became visible exactly as funding and confidence tightened, and social media raised the speed of the run by orders of magnitude.
impact: 美联储推出银行定期融资计划（BTFP），以面值抵押提供一年期资金；签名银行与第一共和银行相继出事，美国国会对 2018 年放宽的监管门槛、未保险存款比例与压力测试展开辩论。全球银行业重新审视持有至到期账户的利率风险披露，「社交媒体挤兑」成为新的监管课题。
impactEn: The Federal Reserve created the Bank Term Funding Program, lending for up to a year against collateral at par; Signature Bank and First Republic followed, and Congress debated the 2018 easing of thresholds, the share of uninsured deposits and stress testing. Banks worldwide revisited disclosure of rate risk in hold-to-maturity books, and 'social media runs' became a standing supervisory topic.
